tool.name: MGnify: FASTQ suffix header check
tool.description: Check whether the strand suffix of a FASTQ file matches the headers inside it
tool.command: #if $input_type.type == "paired_collection" ln -s '$input_type.input.forward' reads_1.fastq.gz && ln -s '$input_type.input.reverse' reads_2.fastq.gz && fastq_suffix_header_check -f reads_1.fastq.gz -r reads_2.fastq.gz -s sample -o ./ #else ln -s '$input_type.input' reads_se.fastq.gz && fastq_suffix_header_check -f reads_se.fastq.gz -s sample -o ./ #end if

param.name: input
param.label: Single-end reads
param.help: Headers are expected to end in /1

param.name: input
param.label: Paired-end reads
param.help: Headers are expected to end in /1 and /2 respectively

tool.help:
**FASTQ suffix header check** -----------------------------
Sanity check (used in the QC stage of the MGnify amplicon pipeline) that the strand suffix implied by the FASTQ **file name** matches the strand suffix in the read **headers**:
- a forward file named ``*_1`` must contain headers ending in ``/1`` - a reverse file named ``*_2`` must contain headers ending in ``/2`` - single-end files are checked against ``/1``
Output ------
A JSON file listing the headers of reads whose suffix does not match (empty file when no errors are found). Use the *empty/not empty* filtering pattern in a workflow to gate downstream steps on this result.
